42323732.clinical_problem: predicting cognitive dysfunction after pediatric posterior fossa tumor surgery
42323732.patient_population: children undergoing posterior fossa tumor surgery, derivation cohort at 3 institutions (2015-2020) and external validation cohort at an independent institution (2021-2023)
42323732.model_description: Uses preoperative multimodal data, including fMRI, DTI, tumor characteristics (volume, midline location), surgical approach, radiotherapy, age, and tumor histology, from children undergoing posterior fossa tumor surgery to predict cognitive dysfunction diagnosed by standardized neuropsychological testing 12 months after surgery. Random forest and LASSO regression models were compared, and the random forest model was translated into a nomogram for clinical risk stratification. Developed on a three-institution retrospective cohort and tested on an independent external cohort.
42323732.dataset_size: multicenter derivation cohort (3 institutions, 2015-2020) in which 172 (28.7%) developed cognitive dysfunction; external validation cohort at an independent institution (2021-2023)
42323732.headline_result: Random forest AUC 0.887 (95% CI 0.87-0.93, derivation) vs LASSO AUC 0.776 (95% CI 0.75-0.80); random forest AUC 0.840 on external validation
42323732.study_design: multicenter retrospective prognostic model development with external validation

42469513.model_family: LightGBM (best of ten compared machine learning architectures), with SHAP interpretability
42469513.clinical_problem: predicting postoperative coronal imbalance after selective posterior thoracic fusion in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
42469513.patient_population: 282 patients with Lenke 1/2 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis treated with selective posterior thoracic fusion
42469513.model_description: Machine learning models take radiographic and clinical predictors, including the spatial relationship between the lowest instrumented vertebra and the last substantially touching vertebra, lumbar curve flexibility (Lumbar Modifier), and Risser grade (skeletal maturity), to predict postoperative coronal imbalance after selective posterior thoracic fusion for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. Ten machine learning architectures were trained after Boruta/LASSO feature selection and compared with SHAP used for interpretability; the best-performing model was LightGBM. The model is intended to support preoperative risk estimation, pending independent external validation.
42469513.study_design: retrospective machine learning model development with internal (split-sample) validation

42715650.clinical_problem: predicting mid-term Cobb angle response to brace treatment in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
42715650.patient_population: 294 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis treated with bracing at two tertiary referral centers
42715650.model_description: A deep learning regression model takes baseline (pre-brace) and early post-brace standing full-spine radiographs, together with age, sex, and Risser stage, and predicts the mid-term Cobb angle for the thoracic and thoracolumbar/lumbar curves in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis treated with bracing. It was developed and cross-validated on a two-center retrospective cohort of 294 patients and externally validated, aiming to support individualized risk stratification and shared decision-making about brace management.
42715650.dataset_size: 294 patients from two tertiary referral centers
42715650.headline_result: Cross-validation MAE 4.06° (T curve, R2=0.811) and 3.75° (TL/L curve, R2=0.746); external validation MAE 5.13° (R2=0.678) and 3.89° (R2=0.723)
42715650.study_design: retrospective multicenter cohort study with external validation

42717246.model_family: Self-supervised vision transformer pretraining (DINOv3 vs DINOv2) and supervised ImageNet initialization, with ViT-B/16 and ConvNeXt-B backbones
42717246.patient_population: pediatric and adult patients across seven chest radiograph datasets (816,183 radiographs total)
42717246.model_description: Benchmarks self-supervised vision transformer pretraining (DINOv3 versus DINOv2) against supervised ImageNet initialization for classifying findings on chest radiographs, using ViT-B/16 and ConvNeXt-B backbones fully fine-tuned at multiple resolutions across seven chest radiograph datasets spanning pediatric and adult cohorts. In adults, DINOv3 became the strongest initialization at 512x512 pixels (especially with ConvNeXt-B), with the largest gains for small, boundary-dependent findings; the pediatric cohort showed no significant benefit from DINOv3, higher resolution, or backbone choice.
42717246.dataset_size: 816,183 radiographs from seven chest radiograph datasets (pediatric and adult cohorts)
42717246.headline_result: DINOv3 with ConvNeXt-B at 512x512 pixels was the strongest adult initialization, with the external-validation advantage preserved; the pediatric cohort showed no significant benefit from DINOv3, higher resolution, or backbone choice
42717246.study_design: retrospective multicenter benchmark study of self-supervised pretraining for chest radiograph classification

42719379.exclusion_reason: Broad thyroid cancer review (molecular biology, treatment, traditional Chinese medicine); AI-assisted ultrasound is a passing mention, not pediatric-focused or the review's subject.

42720764.model_family: Swin Transformer backbone with FiLM-based gestational-age conditioning, multi-task deep learning network
42720764.clinical_problem: fetal growth condition classification (IUGR, gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, amniotic fluid abnormalities) and abdominal landmark detection on obstetric ultrasound
42720764.patient_population: 2,712 pregnant women (18-34 weeks gestation) across three institutions
42720764.model_description: GA-MTNet is a deep learning model with a Swin Transformer backbone and a gestational-age conditioning module that takes an obstetric B-mode ultrasound image plus gestational age as input, and simultaneously detects four fetal abdominal landmarks, classifies five patterns of fetal growth condition (IUGR, gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, normal growth, amniotic fluid abnormalities), and performs biometric regression. It was developed on images from two centers and externally tested at a third center, with an uncertainty-guided continual-learning mechanism for post-deployment adaptation.
42720764.dataset_size: 9,046 B-mode ultrasound images from 2,712 pregnant women; 6,750 images/2,278 patients for development, 1,296 images/434 patients for external test
42720764.headline_result: Internal macro-AUC 0.863, accuracy 84.7%, landmark detection mAP@0.5 0.791; external test set AUC 0.841, accuracy 82.3% (2.2-point AUC drop)
42720764.study_design: retrospective multicenter model development with external validation

42720887.model_family: EfficientNet-B0 with Squeeze-and-Excitation attention (compared against ResNet50, DenseNet121, Swin-Tiny, ConvNeXt-Tiny and CBAM/Coordinate/Parallel Coordinate-Channel attention modules)
42720887.clinical_problem: detecting acute appendicitis on plain abdominal radiographs in children
42720887.patient_population: 162 pediatric patients who underwent surgery for appendicitis and 206 control subjects
42720887.model_description: A deep learning image classifier (EfficientNet-B0 with an added Squeeze-and-Excitation attention module) takes a plain abdominal radiograph, after manual cropping and unsharp-masking preprocessing, and outputs whether the image shows appendicitis. It was trained and evaluated with five-fold stratified cross-validation on radiographs from 162 children with surgically confirmed appendicitis and 206 controls, and Grad-CAM visualizations showed the model attending to the right lower quadrant and pelvic region, the anatomic site of disease.
42720887.dataset_size: 162 appendicitis cases and 206 controls (plain abdominal radiographs)
42720887.headline_result: Best model (EfficientNet-B0 + SE attention) aggregated AUC 0.824 (95% CI 0.781-0.863); baseline EfficientNet-B0 AUC 0.804
42720887.study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with cross-validation

42721356.exclusion_reason: Systematic review of AI for CT-based traumatic brain injury assessment explicitly restricted to adult (≥18 years) patients; pediatric-only cohorts were excluded from the review.

emb:L2044083713.clinical_problem: AI applications across the pediatric and fetal echocardiography imaging pipeline for congenital and pediatric heart disease
emb:L2044083713.patient_population: fetal, pediatric, and adult patients with congenital heart disease undergoing echocardiography
emb:L2044083713.model_description: Narrative review synthesizing 2020-2025 literature on AI (machine learning and deep learning) applied to each step of the pediatric and fetal echocardiography imaging pipeline: image acquisition and quality enhancement, automated view classification, automated measurement and structure segmentation, disease detection/diagnosis including fetal screening, risk stratification, and clinical decision support. No single model is evaluated; the review frames AI as transitioning from a research interest to a clinical instrument in pediatric cardiology.

emb:L2044643867.clinical_problem: AI applications in obstetric/fetal ultrasound: fetal biometry, gestational-age estimation, standard-plane detection, and early detection of congenital abnormalities
emb:L2044643867.model_description: Narrative review of AI (deep learning) applications in obstetric ultrasound, covering automated fetal biometry, gestational-age estimation, standard-plane detection, and early prediction of congenital abnormalities. Reports that in clinical trials, deep learning systems achieved diagnostic performance comparable to experienced sonographers, particularly for routine measurements and image-quality optimization, while generalizability remains limited by variability in ultrasound devices, populations, and acquisition methods.

emb:L2044846270.model_family: multimodal attention fusion framework (CNN image features fused with structured clinical/laboratory data via cross-attention)
emb:L2044846270.clinical_problem: diagnosing acute appendicitis in children using ultrasound plus clinical and laboratory data
emb:L2044846270.patient_population: children in the Regensburg Pediatric Appendicitis Dataset
emb:L2044846270.model_description: A multimodal attention-fusion model combines patient symptoms, laboratory indicators, and ultrasound images to detect pediatric appendicitis. A convolutional neural network extracts image features, clinical variables are encoded as structured inputs, and a cross-attention mechanism fuses the two modalities for final classification. It was trained and evaluated on the public Regensburg Pediatric Appendicitis Dataset.
emb:L2044846270.dataset_size: Regensburg Pediatric Appendicitis Dataset (size not given numerically in the abstract)
emb:L2044846270.headline_result: 97.3% accuracy, 96.5% precision, 97.8% sensitivity, 96.2% specificity, 97.1% F1-score, 96.8% AUROC
emb:L2044846270.study_design: retrospective diagnostic model development on a public dataset

emb:L2045396735.exclusion_reason: Pharmacology review of fenfluramine for refractory childhood epilepsies; no AI or imaging.

emb:L2045453595.exclusion_reason: Narrative review of synaptic pruning and prefrontal neurodevelopment in schizophrenia; no AI/ML model, not imaging-focused.

emb:L2046075251.exclusion_reason: General review of neonatal sepsis/septic shock management; machine learning is a brief passing mention, not focused on diagnostic imaging AI.

emb:L2048155166.exclusion_reason: Systematic review of AI-integrated CT imaging for outcome prediction explicitly restricted to adult traumatic brain injury patients (≥18 years); the review was specifically designed to exclude pediatric populations.

emb:L2048819631.clinical_problem: prenatal detection of congenital heart disease
emb:L2048819631.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal cardiac imaging for congenital heart disease detection
emb:L2048819631.model_description: Narrative review of emerging tools for prenatal congenital heart disease diagnosis: early fetal echocardiography, AI-enabled image acquisition and interpretation, 3D/4D spatiotemporal image correlation with intelligent navigation, and fetal cardiac MRI. These are presented as supplementary tools to conventional 2D fetal echocardiography intended to improve prenatal detection rates, pending further multicenter validation and standardized protocols.

emb:L2048873562.clinical_problem: measuring Graf alpha angle and femoral head coverage for developmental dysplasia of the hip screening in infants
emb:L2048873562.patient_population: 215 infants (309 hips) younger than 6 months undergoing hip ultrasound screening
emb:L2048873562.model_description: AI-assisted software (ZKyK) automatically measures the Graf alpha angle and femoral head coverage on infant hip ultrasound images. Its measurements were compared against manual measurements by senior and junior pediatric orthopedic physicians and trainees using intraclass correlation, Spearman correlation, paired t tests, and Bland-Altman analysis, along with measurement time.
emb:L2048873562.release_evidence: AI-assisted measurements were obtained using the ZKyK software
emb:L2048873562.headline_result: Good agreement between AI-assisted and manual alpha-angle measurements with no statistically significant difference; good-to-excellent inter-observer reliability; AI-assisted analysis required substantially less time than manual measurement
emb:L2048873562.study_design: retrospective diagnostic agreement and reliability study

emb:L2048911807.clinical_problem: AI applications in echocardiography and point-of-care ultrasound, with attention to pediatric and congenital heart disease
emb:L2048911807.patient_population: patients undergoing echocardiography/point-of-care ultrasound, with a section on pediatric and congenital heart disease considerations; strongest evidence base is in adults
emb:L2048911807.model_description: Narrative review of AI applications in echocardiography and point-of-care ultrasound, covering automated left-ventricular segmentation and ejection-fraction estimation, AI-guided image acquisition, and multiview disease-phenotyping models, with a randomized workflow trial cited showing AI-generated ejection-fraction assessment noninferior to sonographer assessment. The review states that pediatric and congenital heart disease applications require age- and anatomy-specific datasets, multicenter validation, and clinician-supervised deployment before adoption.
emb:L2048911807.headline_result: Randomized workflow trial: AI-generated initial ejection-fraction assessment noninferior to sonographer assessment, requiring fewer cardiologist corrections (general/adult evidence base)

emb:L2047641238.exclusion_reason: fNIRS-based autism spectrum disorder classification; fNIRS is not a diagnostic radiology imaging modality.

emb:L2047944299.model_family: hybrid deep-learning framework: multi-scale joint detection, semi-supervised contrastive language-image pretraining for pseudo-labeling, and LDA/normalization-based global attention
emb:L2047944299.clinical_problem: bone age assessment for diagnosing pediatric growth disorders
emb:L2047944299.patient_population: 1,000 public RSNA bone age images and 9,577 additional clinical radiographs
emb:L2047944299.model_description: A deep-learning bone age assessment pipeline combines a multi-scale joint-detection module for the hand and wrist, semi-supervised contrastive language-image pretraining used to generate pseudo-labels for epiphyseal maturity, and an attention-enhanced classification network, producing a continuous bone age estimate from a hand radiograph. It was validated on the public RSNA bone age dataset plus additional clinical radiographs, improving joint-detection rate over a YOLO baseline.
emb:L2047944299.dataset_size: 1,000 public RSNA bone age images and 9,577 clinical radiographs
emb:L2047944299.headline_result: 99.98% joint-detection rate (4.12% improvement over YOLOv10), 81.8% average classification accuracy, mean absolute error 0.25 years, RMSE 0.29 years
emb:L2047944299.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study

emb:L2048005260.model_family: self-supervised learning Vision Transformer with knowledge-distillation pseudo-labeling (domain-specific chest X-ray foundation model)
emb:L2048005260.clinical_problem: chest X-ray foundation model for pneumonia and COVID-19 detection, multi-label disease classification, and lung segmentation
emb:L2048005260.patient_population: adult and pediatric patients across multiple downstream chest radiograph datasets
emb:L2048005260.model_description: DiCoMX is a self-supervised learning framework that pretrains a Vision Transformer on 600,638 unlabeled chest radiographs using pseudo-labels distilled from a teacher model at both the local (token) and global (whole-image) level. The pretrained backbone is then applied to independent downstream tasks including pneumonia and COVID-19 detection in adult and pediatric populations, multi-label disease classification, and lung segmentation, and the pre-training code is publicly released.
emb:L2048005260.release_evidence: The code for pre-training foundation models using DiCoMX is publicly available at: https://github.com/Pediatric-Accelerated-Intelligence-Lab/DiCoMX
emb:L2048005260.dataset_size: 600,638 chest radiographs for pretraining; multiple independent downstream datasets including adult and pediatric cohorts
emb:L2048005260.headline_result: DiCoMX outperforms existing self-supervised learning methods on downstream pneumonia/COVID-19 detection, multi-label classification, and lung segmentation tasks (specific metric values not given in the abstract)
emb:L2048005260.study_design: retrospective technical development and benchmark evaluation

emb:L2048200497.exclusion_reason: General low-dose CT denoising method; pediatric imaging is mentioned only as motivating context, not as part of the evaluated population/dataset.

emb:L2047167201.model_family: YOLOv12-based real-time object detection network, adapted for fetal spinal ultrasound
emb:L2047167201.clinical_problem: detecting vertebral abnormalities (hemivertebrae, butterfly vertebrae, block vertebrae) on prenatal spinal ultrasound
emb:L2047167201.patient_population: 968 images from 735 fetuses (development) and 221 images from 185 fetuses (external test) at two hospitals
emb:L2047167201.model_description: FSU-YOLOv12 is a deep learning object detector adapted from YOLOv12 to detect vertebral abnormalities on fetal spinal ultrasound images, with targeted optimizations to handle small vertebrae, acoustic shadowing, artifacts, and low tissue contrast. It was trained and validated on images from one hospital and independently tested on an external hospital's data, running in real time (149 frames per second) with a lightweight architecture (2.6M parameters).
emb:L2047167201.dataset_size: 968 images from 735 fetuses (development); 221 images from 185 fetuses (external test)
emb:L2047167201.headline_result: mAP(50) 91.9%, mAP(75) 55.9%, mAP 52.3%, precision 94.2%, recall 86.3%, F1 90.1%, 149 fps inference with 2.6M parameters
emb:L2047167201.study_design: retrospective multicenter model development with external test set

emb:L2047404671.model_family: DenseNet-201 backbone with convolutional block attention module (CBAM) and knowledge distillation, staged/progressive training
emb:L2047404671.clinical_problem: classifying first-trimester fetal echocardiography standard views/planes to support early detection of congenital heart defects
emb:L2047404671.patient_population: first-trimester fetuses (12-14 weeks gestation) undergoing fetal echocardiography
emb:L2047404671.model_description: A three-phase progressive learning framework built on a DenseNet-201 backbone enhanced with a convolutional block attention module and knowledge distillation classifies first-trimester fetal echocardiography standard views/planes, addressing the challenge of underdeveloped cardiac structures and probe-movement variability at this gestational stage. Training proceeds in stages, from clear to deformed to the full image set, to progressively improve generalization on a minority, harder-to-classify view class, with the aim of supporting earlier detection of fetal heart defects.
emb:L2047404671.headline_result: 3% and 1% overall accuracy/metric improvement over state-of-the-art baselines; approximately 5% recall and 3% F1 improvement for the minority X-sign view class
emb:L2047404671.study_design: retrospective technical development and benchmark evaluation
